document.title: Senior Interagency Group Meeting on Follow-up to the visit of Indian Prime Minister Gandhi, June 20
document.authors: Senior Interagency Group (chaired by Under Secretary Armacost)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Summary of conclusions from the SIG meeting after Gandhi's first Washington visit (June 11-15). The U.S. saw a chance for a new stage in relations and to wean India from reliance on the USSR. It welcomed Gandhi's interest in a more active role on Afghanistan and proposed briefing the Indians on U.S.-Soviet talks and Cordovez negotiations.

key_claims: US officials judged that India appeared willing to play a more active role on Afghanistan, though its seriousness was unclear.
Gandhi's dispatch of Foreign Secretary Bhandari to Moscow was viewed as a possible positive sign.
The US planned to brief India on US-Soviet and UN (Cordovez) talks on Afghanistan and ensure Pakistan also briefed India.
A later checklist noted no change in India's public position on Afghanistan despite continued dialogue.
